design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (rental_coordination_desk). Round 1 built the task; round 2 (policy-task audit rework) is recorded at the end.
DRAW: draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 4, 4]}; assignment: rental_ext_delay_goodwill 5, rental_ext_repair_customer_discount 5, rental_ext_time_charge_correction 4, rental_ext_young_renter_fee 4.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT: nothing was occupied before task 0. Task 0 claims the customer-pay settlement credits and fee (billing-error credit, repair-customer discount credit, young-renter fee, delay goodwill credit; tools credit_rental_billing_error_4d32ac17, credit_repair_customer_discount_d339b3bd, charge_young_renter_fee_a6a6d206, accept_rental_goodwill_credit_52804ea3). Task 1 holds the coverage side of an insurance rental (network courtesy days, insurer extension, self-pay days charge) - disjoint events and tools.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the customer asks only for amends for lost rental days. The goodwill rule is not fixed until the repair-customer discount stands against the time charge, and only after the young-renter fee stands as a charge; the discount is worked out only after any overcharge on the time charge stands credited as a billing error. The agent must find that the partner's posted time charge (18 calendar days x 42.99 = 773.82) is wrong, rebuild it from the reservation's pickup/return times with weekly blocks, a long-rental block rate, a remainder rule and a standing extra-day rate read from the warranty and claim desks, then book the discount and the young-renter fee and hand the goodwill acceptance to the customer; the goodwill values a lost day by the net time charge over the days it rightly covers and uplifts it by the repair order's discount program.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root rental_ext_delay_goodwill (user tool accept_rental_goodwill_credit_52804ea3). Edges (all value_input, state form): (1) repair_customer_discount -> time_charge_correction, gate discount_base_amount, affirmative sentence "The repair-customer discount is worked out only after any amount by which the time charge was posted above the rental's correct time charge stands credited against it as a billing error." - only the billing-error policy books a billing_error credit; unresolved: rental_ledger.8e093547-c1d0-48d5-b4ad-555b8a43466e is the only ledger row (773.82 for 18 days), corrected charge 546.00. (2) delay_goodwill -> repair_customer_discount, gate lost_day_time_value, negated sentence "A goodwill credit for lost rental days is not fixed until the repair-customer discount owed on the time charge stands against it." - unresolved: no credit row. (3) delay_goodwill -> young_renter_fee, gate lost_day_fee_value, affirmative sentence "The goodwill credit for lost rental days is fixed only after every young-renter fee the renter owes on the rental stands as a charge on it." - unresolved: renter_age 22, no young_renter charge. Each sentence carries an ordering connective, a record-visible state, no tool/id/code token, and the edge's exact scope. Order: billing error -> discount -> young-renter fee -> goodwill; the young-renter branch shares no input with the discount branch, and replaying it first gives the identical terminal hash and goodwill (authoring run).
EDGE DELETION SENSITIVITY (handling-time replays): skip billing error -> discount 204.83 instead of 144.53; skip discount -> goodwill 100.06 instead of 82.21; skip young-renter fee -> goodwill 49.59 instead of 82.21.
FACTOR CARD (handling-time worlds, recomputed with check_compute's build_env/eval_compute):
rental_ext_time_charge_correction = 227.82 (all-baseline 42.99): time_charge_structure baseline -> 42.99; remainder_pricing baseline -> 203.85; long_rental_block_rate baseline -> 178.82; standing_extra_day_rate baseline -> 203.85
rental_ext_repair_customer_discount = 144.53 (all-baseline 77.38): discount_base_choice baseline -> 204.83; repair_period_share baseline -> 163.8; overrun_discount_rate baseline -> 96.35; calibration_points baseline -> 120.44; program_points baseline -> 120.44
rental_ext_young_renter_fee = 264.0 (all-baseline 425.0): weekly_fee_days baseline -> 360.0; age_span_daily_fee baseline -> 220.0; calibration_hold_days baseline -> 312.0; booking_reliability_reduction baseline -> 330.0
rental_ext_delay_goodwill = 82.21 (all-baseline 18.92): calibration_delay_days baseline -> 123.31; goodwill_authority_tier baseline -> 41.1; lost_day_time_basis baseline -> 79.45; delay_goodwill_share baseline -> 41.1; program_uplift baseline -> 78.29
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: credits (rental_customer_credit) are governed by rental_evt_customer_settlement only (no gate -> policy_scope); the young-renter charge (rental_customer_charge) by rental_evt_settlement_split (gate rental_returned: reservation 72537456-1f8f-42d8-9c08-72ad84c63e87 status returned) and rental_evt_options_and_fees (no gate). No time gate. Declared overrides, each quoting the base sentence: settlement_split's customer-pay weekly sentence and discount sentence, class_and_renter's young-renter fee sentence, customer_settlement's goodwill cap sentence, and rental_days' return-grace sentence in all four policies (rental days here are whole days plus one when the return time as counted is later than the pickup time of day).
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: reservation 72537456-1f8f-42d8-9c08-72ad84c63e87 (Compact Rental, customer_pay, tied to the retail repair); all credits name the one time charge 8e093547-c1d0-48d5-b4ad-555b8a43466e; the closed 2025 claim repair and the active warranty are standing evidence only; the calibration order is the one opened for the retail repair.
SEED ROWS: profile; Mazda3 (forward camera); closed Standard Claim Repair (2025) and its active Collision Lifetime warranty; converted Drive-In Estimate booking, no no-show; closed Bumper Refinish Service started 2026-09-14, ready 2026-09-25, released 2026-09-28 (target 2 business days -> overrun 7); Static Camera Calibration with failed in-house attempts 2026-09-17 and 2026-09-18, sublet 2026-09-18, completed 2026-09-19; the rental (pickup 2026-09-14 08:10, after-hours key drop counted 2026-10-01 07:30 -> 17 rental days) and the partner's final time charge for 18 calendar days. Near-misses: 18 posted vs 17 rental days; ready date vs release date; the second failed attempt vs the first.
PERSONA DESIGN: Marcus volunteers only the goal and seed-backed facts; phone + PIN on request; passive agreement to other entries; runs the acceptance only with the values handed over; no line points at a billing error, discount or fee.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate+verify, eleven reads, billing-error credit 227.82, discount 144.53, young-renter charge 264.00 booked for 11 charged fee days, goodwill acceptance 82.21 on time charge 8e093547-c1d0-48d5-b4ad-555b8a43466e.
DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT: the published rules and lookups give the same four amounts (227.82, 144.53, 264.00, 82.21) and the young-renter charge's day count (the rule names the charged fee days); every tier condition is disjoint and every rounding point stated.
ROUND 2 REWORK (audit items): T0-1 - the unoccupiable day-count factor was removed (rental days are a plain count) and a remainder_pricing method factor was added to the billing-error computation; its round-2 fall-through applied only to an empty remainder, which round 3 corrected (see below). T0-2 - the young-renter age ladder's out-of-scope tier is replaced by a reachable short-span surcharge tier (under_23_short_surcharge_usd). T0-3 - see round 3. T0-4 - the young-renter rule states that the charge is booked for its charged fee days, so days_count is 11 (was 17); the amount is unchanged. CG-4 - the loyalty test is an exact existence test (a closed network claim repair). CG-5 - every rental-day count declares the base return-grace sentence superseded. Latent fixes: guarded retail/calibration reads, hold-days rule names the completion date, goodwill scope names the customer-pay repair, goodwill delay days stated as a date difference, persona no longer says the invoice looked high.
ROUND 3 REWORK (audit items): R2-1 - remainder_pricing's tiers are now a remainder of weekly_rate_threshold_days or more (one more block) / two to fewer than weekly_rate_threshold_days (extra-day rate, capped) / a single remaining day or none (partner rate per day); the fall-through prices a real single extra day, so the billing-error computation has four real factors: time_charge_structure, remainder_pricing, long_rental_block_rate, standing_extra_day_rate. Gold 227.82 unchanged. R2-2 - lost_day_time_basis is re-cut on what stands at goodwill's handling time (the discount credit always does): a billing-error credit stands (net charge over rental days) / no billing-error credit but a corrected time charge (net corrected charge over its days) / otherwise (net final charge over the posted days, the standard). O-6 - the lost-day fee basis factor, whose middle tier existed only when the young-renter prerequisite was skipped, is no longer a factor: the fee value is the young-renter charge over the rental days (zero when none), and a program_uplift parameter factor (military / returning_customer / none, values from the repair tier) takes its slot. Goodwill gold 78.29 -> 82.21; all-baseline 21.50 -> 18.92.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Lindqvist, 22, a line cook in Minneapolis who talks fast and a bit fed up but stays polite. Crestline refinished the rear bumper on your 2018 Mazda3 hatchback as a job you paid for yourself, and while it was in the shop you rented a compact car through Crestline's rental desk, also on your own card. You dropped the Mazda off and picked up the rental on September 14. The shop's camera calibration on your car went wrong twice and they had to send the car to the Mazda dealer, and the whole job dragged on; you got the car back on September 28 and dropped the rental in the after-hours key box the night of September 30.

You are calling because you paid for rental days that only happened because the shop's own calibration problems held your car up, and you want Crestline to make those lost rental days right on your rental. That is the one thing you are asking for; you are not asking for a refund of the repair itself, and you are fine with the rental days you kept on your own after you had the Mazda back.

You start by explaining that in your own words. When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number, 6125550347, and when asked for a second detail you give your account PIN, 3817. If asked for your email, it is marcus.lindqvist@outlook.com, and your ZIP code is 55406. If the agent asks which rental or which car, it is the compact you rented for the bumper job on the Mazda3; you do not know any reference numbers by heart. If asked how old you were when you picked the car up, you say 22. You remember the bumper job came with a discount because you had your car fixed at Crestline last year, but you do not know any figures from the rental invoice, and if the agent quotes a number you only say whether it sounds plausible or that you would like it checked against the record.

If the agent tells you that other entries on the rental have to be put right or added before the amends can be worked out, you say that is fine and to go ahead, and you do not argue with an added fee you agreed to in the rental contract. Once the agent tells you the amount Crestline can offer and hands you the step to accept it, you accept it yourself using exactly the reservation reference, charge reference and amount the agent gives you, and you read back what the confirmation says. After that you thank the agent and end the call; you do not raise anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The young-renter fee is parallel to the billing-error -> discount chain. Its write is a separate charge row and none of the three earlier policies reads the other's entry (the discount base reads only time-charge and billing-error rows). Replaying young-renter first, then billing error, discount and goodwill gives the identical terminal DB hash (authoring run: True) and the identical goodwill 82.21. The billing-error -> discount -> goodwill order is fixed by the two prerequisite sentences.
